Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
The LOD scores from fitqtl (with a single QTL model) and scanone should be the same if both are based on the same method.

LOD scores in the first step of stepwiseqtl should be the same as scanone if both are using the same method.  LOD scores in subsequent steps will be different as they are conditional on earlier QTL.

If you have examples that indicate problems, I would like to hear more.

karl

Previously, I use argument "use=complete.obs" for multiple-phenotype one
QTL genome scan.

scanone and stepwise become consistent.
The number does matter.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] sim.cross output: data vs. truegeno
messages.body_plain:
The simulation of 8-way RIL data in R/qtl is still "developmental".  We're still working out how best to encode the data, and so aspects of this are particularly awkward at the moment.  Nevertheless..

In the geno portion of the output of sim.cross for type="ri8sib",

  data = matrix of snp genotypes with special encoding that indicates compatibility with founder strains' genotypes
  truegeno = matrix of underlying 'true' genotypes (coded 1-8, indicating the 8 founder strains)

In the absence of genotyping errors or missing data, the simplest approach to get the SNP genotypes would be to pull out the founders' SNPs using the 'truegeno' information, as follows:

set.seed(85238087)
map <- sim.map(50, n.mar=26, eq.spacing=TRUE, include.x=FALSE)
fsnps <- simFounderSnps(map, n.str="8")
x <- sim.cross(map, n.ind=10, type="ri8sib", founderGeno=fsnps)

trueg <- x$geno[[1]]$truegeno
snpg <- trueg
for(i in 1:nrow(trueg))
  for(j in 1:ncol(trueg))
    snpg[i,j] <- fsnps[[1]][j,trueg[i,j]]

With potential errors or missing data, it's best to use the 'data' component (which includes simulated errors and missing data).  In this case, look at whether the data are compatible with the "first" strain, and then pull out the SNP genotype for that strain.

sameas1 <- x$geno[[1]]$data %% 2
sameas1[is.na <http://is.na>(sameas1)] <- 0
snpg2 <- sameas1
for(i in 1:nrow(sameas1)) {
  for(j in 1:ncol(sameas1)) {
    if(sameas1[i,j])
     snpg2[i,j] <- fsnps[[1]][j,x$cross[i,1]]
    else
     snpg2[i,j] <- 1-fsnps[[1]][j,x$cross[i,1]]
  }
}
snpg2[is.na <http://is.na>(x$geno[[1]]$data)] <- NA

karl

You need to infer phase, and there's a complicated encoding described in the help file for read.cross (in the section "Value" under "geno".

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
messages.body_plain:
First, if the two progenitors are heterozygous, then the F1 individuals are not genetically identical which leads to population structure among the F2 individuals that needs to be taken into account. If you don't, you run a serious risk of false positive evidence for QTL.

Second, if there are many markers/regions that are not of the AA:BB type, then by throwing out such regions, you are first throwing away much of your ability to map QTL in such regions.

If at *all* loci that affect the phenotype, the two progenitors are fixed (like AA, BB), then it would be okay to treat the whole cross like a simple intercross between two inbred lines, but if the progenitors are heterozygous for some QTL, you need to deal with these complexities.

karl
